evidence.sectionTitle: Freedom, certainty, prevalence, and the goods of hiddenness

card.critique: Strongest feature: Sechler identifies conversation, Christian fellowship, confession, and shared inquiry as goods occasioned by uncertainty, making his reply relevant to Clifton’s challenge and consistent with the precision-and-clarity score of 74. Principal limitation: He contrasts hiddenness with one-hundred-percent certainty, while Clifton questions whether settled awareness of God permits choice, and he never establishes that reflection would disappear rather than acquire different subjects, fitting the evidence-warrant score of 50. Live burden: Sechler needs to explain why divine availability specifically eliminates these investigative goods, and why comparable cooperation could not flourish in a nonhidden world. Locked score: The overall 63 reflects a clear possibility that answers the exchange, tempered by an unproven necessity claim and an overstated contrast.

fields.currentValue: Other valuable activities would replace hiddenness-dependent inquiry This rests on Clifton argues those activities are contingently useful responses to hiddenness; a nonhidden world would permit different valuable projects.

evidence.sectionTitle: Freedom, certainty, prevalence, and the goods of hiddenness

card.critique: Strongest feature: Clifton challenges the proposed value of hiddenness by distinguishing a conversation’s conditional usefulness from intrinsic value, then argues that a nonhidden world could contain worthwhile conversations, supporting the responsiveness score of 94. Principal limitation: His replacement-goods claim remains asserted rather than demonstrated, because he supplies no examples or account showing that alternative projects would preserve the relational benefits Sechler names, which helps explain the evidence-warrant score of 63. Live burden: Clifton needs to show why changed background facts would reliably generate comparable or greater fellowship and inquiry, rather than merely ending the present discussion. Locked score: The overall 84 reflects an exceptionally direct and coherent reply whose counterfactual is plausible but still needs substantive support.
